question: A student is asked to list the components of a standard 12-lead ECG recording. Which of the following best describes the standard lead set captured on a routine ECG?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basic principles of the 12-lead ECG

options.text: Three standard limb leads, three augmented limb leads, six precordial leads
options.rationale: Correct because the lecture states a 12-lead ECG includes 3 standard limb, 3 augmented limb, and 6 precordial leads.

options.text: Four limb leads and eight precordial leads on routine tracing
options.rationale: Wrong because the lecture specifies three standard limb and three augmented limb leads rather than four limb leads; changing to three limb and three augmented would make it correct.

options.text: Twelve identical chest leads placed across the anterior thorax
options.rationale: Wrong because the lecture distinguishes limb and precordial leads; if the leads were described as different views rather than identical chest leads it could be correct.

options.text: Six limb leads only without precordial chest leads recorded
options.rationale: Wrong because the lecture emphasizes six precordial leads are part of the standard 12‑lead; adding the six precordial leads would make this correct.

options.text: Three augmented limb leads only with no standard limb leads
options.rationale: Wrong because augmented limb leads supplement but do not replace the three standard limb leads; including both sets would make it correct.

options.text: One second per large block at standard speed
options.rationale: Wrong because one second equals five large blocks per the lecture; if counting five large blocks this option would be correct.
